title: Books for Many People
paragraphs: Long ago in Europe, people made books by hand. A writer copied every page with a pen, one letter at a time. One book could take months, so books were rare and very expensive. Few people could afford to own books.

In the fifteenth century, a German man named Johannes Gutenberg changed this. He built a printing press that used small metal letters. The letters could be moved and used again and again. Workers put them in lines, covered them with ink, and pressed paper on top. Now a shop could make many copies of the same page in one day.

Gutenberg was not the first person to print with movable letters. People in Korea had done it with metal letters earlier. But his press spread quickly across Europe. Books became cheaper, and more people learned to read. New ideas about religion and learning could now travel much faster than before.
